title: Investor Behavior and the Benefits of Dispersed Stock Ownership

scopes.description: Complete current documented target: the supplied primary-analysis program plus the published exploratory online appendix branch. The appendix time-series input/producer contract remains unverified.

Primary Stata tables from the author-supplied BCH Data Sheet workbook, retaining the included cleaning, within-university standardization, treatment interactions, and both executed Table 3 model variants. This narrower scope excludes the published exploratory online-appendix branch.

requirements.description: The author-prepared BCH Data Sheet workbook is the row-level analysis dataset named in the data description. Its raw first-sheet headers include all base variables consumed by the supplied main Stata program. The documented Qualtrics, hand-coded poll, and Starbucks purchase records are historical inputs to this already-supplied dataset, not separate live dependencies for this analysis route. The bounded probe confirms readability and headers only; full row population/coverage is not established by that one-row probe.

routes.description: Workbook is present in the package; the bounded first-sheet probe reports 276 raw headers, all 37 directly consumed base fields are present, headers are unique and Stata-valid, and the sheet name is BCH Data Sheet. The Stata entry line still needs an Excel import statement because it currently uses an empty use path.

requirements.description: The full target includes the appendix investment-salience time-series branch. It requires an author-compatible university-by-treatment-group-week panel of 94 observations, with the weekly outcome TotalSpend (defined as OwnMoney at that aggregation level) and reminder overlap flags Salient_1week and Salient_2weeks. The package does not specify the input period, weekly source, reminder-date/event construction, or an executable panel producer. The supplied participant workbook is only a candidate because its probed participant fields do not verify the 94-row weekly aggregation or event flags.

routes.description: Candidate input only: the bounded workbook probe confirms participant-level University, Treatment, and OwnMoney headers, but not a weekly index, the university-by-treatment-group-week aggregation, 94 observations, or salience-event coverage. No supplied producer creates this panel.

software.name: Stata
software.description: Stata 18 is available in the supplied environment probe. The supplied program uses standard Stata commands including egen standardization, regression/test commands, bayesmh, and bayesgraph.

software.name: outreg2
software.description: Required by the supplied program to export Table 4 and Table 5 regression results. It was not found in the checked default or shared Stata ado paths; a repository package route is documented, but this audit did not install it.

issues.description: Line 6 is use "" with no path. The only packaged dataset is BCH Data Sheet.xlsx, so the current Stata command does not load the supplied Excel workbook. The data description names this workbook as the final dataset and the bounded probe confirms its sheet and consumed headers; the missing step is an explicit Excel import (or an author-specified Stata-format file/path).

The first outreg2 export for each Table 4 outcome panel writes to table4_reg with replace (lines 129, 144, 159). Thus the OthersMoney panel resets the OwnMoney export and the RegulatoryAlignment panel resets the OthersMoney export; only the final panel remains at that shared output base.

The published appendix reports an investment-salience time-series analysis at the university-group-week level but the supplied main Stata code ends with Bayesian Table 7 analyses and contains no weekly panel producer or appendix analysis entry point. The candidate participant workbook does not establish the required 94-observation group-week panel, weekly outcome construction, or reminder-event flags. The exact prepared input or author-provided producer contract is unresolved; do not derive it independently.

The full target also includes the appendix analyses by university and the documented Income, NumberInvestments, and US-national subsamples. The supplied Stata program contains the main-table workflow but no corresponding appendix subgroup analysis entry point or output instructions. The appendix identifies the subgroup definitions and reports results, but the package does not supply an executable procedure for these branches. Obtain the author workflow/specification; do not invent or independently implement regression code. The weekly time-series data/producer gap is tracked separately.

evidence.description: The data description identifies BCH Data Sheet as the final dataset and BCH Stata Code as the conversion and primary-analysis program.
evidence.quote:
5. Code to Convert Raw Data into the Final Dataset

The Stata code to convert the raw data into the final dataset and conduct the primary
analyses is available on the JAR website. The Stata code file name is “BCH Stata Code.”
The file name of our final dataset is “BCH Data Sheet.”

evidence.description: Qualtrics, the hand-coded mid-term polls, and Starbucks card purchase records are described as the historical sources used to create the packaged final dataset.
evidence.quote:
The primary data source for the paper is Qualtrics, an online platform that study
participants used to complete our main survey instrument. We also obtained data from
two other sources. First, we hand coded students’ responses to the mid-term poll, which
was administered on paper. Second, we obtained data on participants’ Starbucks Card
purchases directly from a representative at Starbucks, pursuant to a study participation
agreement described in Item 3 below.

observations. Because this is a relatively small sample size, we caution interpreting the results

Salient_1week equals one for each week that overlaps with the date the investment reminder

evidence.quote:

evidence.description: The supplied main code Table 7 section runs Bayesian analyses, separate from the appendix weekly time-series branch.
evidence.quote:
***TABLE 7: Bayesian analysis***
set seed 14
bayesmh OwnMoney Treatment if Include == 1, likelihood(normal({var})) prior({OwnMoney: _cons}, flat) prior ({OwnMoney: Treatment}, normal(0,10)) prior({var}, jeffreys)
bayesgraph diagnostics _all

review_notes: The frozen dependency checklist contains zero entries; manual inspection of actual Stata reads, generated variables, software calls, and output branches was still required. The main program has one blank top-level input statement and no additional file reads, merges, or raw-source acquisition commands.

The supplied workbook probe read one row for metadata and found 276 unique Stata-valid raw headers; all 37 base fields directly consumed by the main code appear. The probe does not establish full row coverage or population fidelity.

The data description documents Qualtrics surveys, manually coded paper-poll responses, and Starbucks purchase records as historical construction sources for the supplied final workbook. They are not treated as separate live execution inputs for the supplied analysis routes.
Both the original and alternative Table 3 command sections execute in sequence; the cortesti call is inside a block comment and is not a required add-on.

The only required nonbuilt-in Stata command identified for the primary program is outreg2. It is absent from the checked default/shared ado paths. Table 4 panel exports replace the same target at lines 129, 144, and 159; the proposal retargets all seven calls in each later outcome panel.

The campaign full_pipeline includes the published exploratory appendix: both its 94-observation university-by-treatment-group-week time-series and its university-specific and Income/NumberInvestments/US-national subgroup analyses. The weekly input/producer contract and subgroup program/output instructions are not supplied; each remains a distinct full-scope issue. The analysis_only scope is limited to the supplied primary program and author-prepared workbook.
